cards.text: Just before this, the daughters of Jerusalem, the women of the city, asked where the beloved had gone, and the answer came back: down to his garden (Song of Solomon 6:1-2). Now the song speaks to "my darling" and starts praising her. Grab a seat, friend, because the compliments are about to come FAST.

cards.question: The song tells her she's as beautiful as Tirzah, a city in Israel (1 Kings 15:33). Which other city does the song say she's as lovely as?

cards.text: Then the song says she's as majestic as troops with banners. Not a flower, friend. Not a sunset. An ARMY!

cards.question: Next the song asks her to turn her eyes away, because her eyes have ___ the speaker.
Then the song compares her hair to something coming from Gilead, a region east of the Jordan. What is it?

cards.text: Now her teeth, like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing. Nobody's ever praised MY teeth, friend, because all I've got is a mustache and a dream.

cards.question: When the song says each of her teeth has its twin and not one is lost, it's picturing a full matched set with nothing missing.

cards.text: Then the song says her brow behind her veil is like a slice of pomegranate. Friend, I'm standing here blushing, and none of it was even about ME.
Now the song brings up a crowd: sixty queens, eighty concubines and maidens without number.

cards.question: But next to all those queens, concubines and maidens, the song says "my dove, my perfect one" is ___.
The song says this dove is the favorite of the mother who bore her.

cards.text: Now the maidens, the queens and the concubines all get a look at this dove. That's a LOT of eyes, friend, and I'd be sweating flour.

cards.question: When the maidens see this dove, what do they do?
Like the maidens, the queens and concubines praise this dove.

cards.text: Then the song asks, "Who is this…" Friend, that's what you say when somebody walks into a room and every head turns.

cards.question: The song asks who this is who shines. What does the song compare this shining one to?

cards.text: The dawn, the moon, the sun and the stars in procession. Berry, one of my cookie cutter kids, the little star who watched the night sky from the kitchen window every night, would've LOVED this one.
Then the song says, "I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley…"

cards.question: At the walnut grove, the speaker went to see if the vines were ___ or the pomegranates were in bloom.

cards.text: Then the song says desire set the speaker among the royal chariots of their people. Walnut blossoms to royal CHARIOTS, friend. Talk about a change of scenery.

cards.question: The speaker who went down to the walnut grove knew all along that their desire would set them among the royal chariots.
